Summarizing our derivation, we first used a system's physical symmetries to define a transpose-like matrix operation that translates the physical symmetries to matrix symmetries of the system's H, X, and Y.

Then,

we found a change of basis that transformed this matrix operation into the standard matrix transpose, such that in this atypical basis the system's operators were either symmetric or skew-symmetric. Finally, by tensoring these operators using the Pauli matrices, we formed a single skew-symmetric matrix whose Pfaffian's sign discriminates between which atomic limits a given system can be connected to without closing the system's local gap. Altogether, by using results from matrix homotopy; this argument yields an energy-resolved invariant for classifying fragile topology as well as a quantitative measure of topological protection.
